article.title: Firefox 160: Desktop On-Device SpeechRecognition in 40 Languages, an Early-Version Mini Window; MDN Says a WebTransport Change Needs Code Updates
article.summary: Mozilla's Firefox 160, released November 10, 2026, supports on-device SpeechRecognition on desktop in 40 languages and adds an early-version Mini Window; MDN lists WebTransport changes.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Mozilla released Firefox 160 on November 10, 2026, according to its [release notes](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/160.0/releasenotes/) and [MDN's developer notes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/160). The release adds a Mini Window feature that Mozilla calls an "early version" and a "Never allow" button for sites that repeatedly ask to handle mailto: links. For web developers, MDN lists on-device speech recognition through the Web Speech API on desktop, several WebTransport changes, and a new CSS alias. [LWN.net](https://lwn.net/Articles/1106542/), [OMG! Ubuntu](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/11/firefox-160-released-mini-window) and [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Firefox-160-adds-mini-windows-and-on-device-speech-recognition-11521432.html) each reported the release, and their feature lists differ in places, as noted below. An earlier Herald article covered [Firefox 159](/article/2026-11/07-firefox-159-enables-scroll-driven-animations-by-default-and-adds-scoped-custom-element-registries-webdev-lists-both-as-baseline-newly-available).

## Speech recognition

Mozilla's [release notes](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/160.0/releasenotes/) say the SpeechRecognition interface of the Web Speech API is now supported, "providing on-device, real-time speech-to-text in 40 languages." [MDN's developer notes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/160) give the scope: the feature is "now available on desktop," and "Recognition is not supported on Android, and neither is remote (cloud) recognition." The firefox.com release notes do not state the desktop-only scope.

MDN's [guide to the Web Speech API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Speech_API/Using_the_Web_Speech_API) describes how pages ask for on-device processing. A page sets the `processLocally` property, which defaults to false, to true. The guide says on-device recognition requires a one-time language pack download for each language, after which it is available offline. If `processLocally` is true and the language pack is missing, `start()` fails with a `language-not-supported` error, and pages can check for packs with `SpeechRecognition.available()` and install them with `SpeechRecognition.install()`. According to the guide, the `on-device-speech-recognition` Permissions-Policy, whose default allowlist is `self`, controls those two methods. The guide describes the API generally and is not specific to Firefox.

[heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Firefox-160-adds-mini-windows-and-on-device-speech-recognition-11521432.html) says users "must first download an AI model for recognition" and that recognition afterwards works without an internet connection, with the website receiving the recognized text. MDN's guide calls the download a language pack; neither source explains the difference in wording. As of November 13, 2026, MDN's [SpeechRecognition reference page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SpeechRecognition) carries a "Limited availability" label and says the feature is not Baseline because it does not work in some of the most widely-used browsers.

## WebTransport and other platform changes

[MDN's developer notes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/160) list these changes, among others:

- **WebTransport:** the `WebTransport()` constructor accepts a `headers` option that adds custom HTTP headers to the extended CONNECT request, and the server's response headers are available in `WebTransport.responseHeaders`. The constructor also supports a `datagramsReadableType` option; set to `bytes`, it makes the incoming datagram stream a readable byte stream.
- **A change MDN says needs code updates:** `WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial()` now requires a `context` argument and takes a new `outputLength` argument; previously, MDN says, the method always returned 32 bytes. MDN says code that omits either argument will need to be updated.
- **Renamed buffering properties:** `incomingMaxBufferedDatagrams` and `outgoingMaxBufferedDatagrams` are supported and replace the non-standard `incomingHighWaterMark` and `outgoingHighWaterMark`, which MDN says have been removed.
- **CSS:** `::-webkit-input-placeholder` is supported as an alias of `::placeholder`, which Mozilla's [release notes](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/160.0/releasenotes/) say is meant to improve compatibility with sites that use it.
- **Removal:** the non-standard `MozScrolledAreaChanged` event is no longer dispatched to web pages; setting the `layout.scrolled-area-changed.content.enabled` preference to true restores it.
- **Extensions:** `runtime.PlatformInfo` now returns `arm64` rather than `aarch64` for ARM64 platforms, which MDN says aligns Firefox with Chrome.

MDN also lists five features that ship in Firefox 160 but are disabled by default (the count is the Herald's, from the page's headings): render blocking, lazy loading for video and audio, the `Speculation-Rules` header, `CSSNumericValue` arithmetic methods, and the Canvas 2D `colorSpace` option. MDN says the header is enabled by default in Nightly and the arithmetic methods are supported in Nightly. For the canvas option, MDN says pixel data is not yet converted between color spaces, so `getImageData()` returns the same pixels whichever color space is requested.

## Browser features

The [release notes](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/160.0/releasenotes/) describe Mini Window as moving "a tab or a selected part of a page into an always-on-top window while browsing" and ask for feedback on "this early version of the feature." [LWN](https://lwn.net/Articles/1106542/) says it is "in early development," while [OMG! Ubuntu](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/11/firefox-160-released-mini-window) says it "is in beta." OMG! Ubuntu describes opening it from the tab context menu or the toolbar, and [heise online](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Firefox-160-adds-mini-windows-and-on-device-speech-recognition-11521432.html) gives a dashboard section kept visible while working in other tabs as an example.

The [release notes](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/160.0/releasenotes/) also list a Picture-in-Picture playback speed setting from 0.25x to 2.0x that appears only when the player window is medium-sized or larger; a "Never allow" button for sites that repeatedly ask to handle mailto: and other links; playback of Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3 or PCM audio; and WebGL rendering through Apple's Metal API on macOS, which Mozilla says "can improve performance on some sites." Other entries cover dragging history entries to the tab strip, a "Paste and Search" menu label, MathML accessibility in saved PDFs and Organize Tabs in French for Smart Window, which the notes say is part of a progressive roll out. Fixes include a freeze of several seconds when signing in to intranet sites using NTLM or Kerberos authentication. The notes also list "Various security fixes"; this article does not assess them.

## Where the accounts differ

[OMG! Ubuntu's](https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/11/firefox-160-released-mini-window) list of other changes includes "US users can now access the Yahoo! Scout in the chatbot sidebar." The en-US and en-GB [release notes](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/160.0/releasenotes/) and [MDN's developer notes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/160), as read on November 13, 2026, contain no mention of Yahoo or Scout, and neither does [LWN's brief](https://lwn.net/Articles/1106542/) or [heise online's article](https://www.heise.de/en/news/Firefox-160-adds-mini-windows-and-on-device-speech-recognition-11521432.html). The sources do not explain the difference, and the Herald could not confirm the item.

## What the sources do not say

None of the cited sources says when Mini Window will move beyond its early stage, or what a page that does not set `processLocally` experiences in Firefox 160, where [MDN says](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/160) remote recognition is not supported.
